Last week we partnered with @thehabura , @sephardicbrotherhood , @americansephardifed and @orthodoxunion for the inaugural Sephardic Rabbinic Conference, which brought together over 50 distinguished rabbis and communal leaders from across North America, and six other countries for two days of dialogue, vision, and collaboration at the Orthodox Union headquarters in Downtown Manhattan. 

Several rabbis and educators from our community were in attendance, serving as panelists and thought-leaders throughout the sessions. On Sunday night, the Kahal was treated to a spirited musical celebration of our rich heritage featuring, among others, Benny Zalta, Mark Faiena, and Rabbi Jack Varon. The keynote address was delivered by Rabbi Joseph Dweck, Senior Rabbi of the Spanish & Portuguese Community of the United Kingdom.

17911732791151486.caption:
Since the start of Operation Rising Lions, we’ve been in constant communication with both participants and parents of our Birthright trip—ensuring everyone is safe, informed, and supported every step of the way.

What happened last night reminded us that even in uncertain times, we can still show up for others in powerful ways.

We were originally scheduled to host a BBQ for soldiers on a base in the south. Of course now, due to security concerns, we couldn’t go. But this was never about us—it was always about lifting the spirits of those on the front lines. So the BBQ still happened, just without the group physically there.

The unit they were meant to visit is playing a key role in the current war. They sent a beautiful, heartfelt message back to the girls, thanking them for standing with them even from afar.

Now, we’re hoping to do the same for the BBQ for another base—but we’re still short $1,200. If you want to be part of something that truly lifts up our soldiers when they need it most, the link to donate is in our bio.  #SCAYoungAdults #StandWithIsrael #AmYisraelHai #mayanotisrael #birthrightisrael 🇮🇱

18006124250603813.caption:
The third day of our birthright trip was packed with fun activities and meaningful moments! 

We started the day off with a delicious breakfast at the hotel. Before beginning our first activity of the day, we picked up a group of Israeli soldiers who are joining us for the trip! The soldiers are all so friendly and we can’t wait to get to know them all better. ‘

With the Israelis in tow, we made our way to our first activity: rafting on the Jordan River! It was so fun splashing each other and taking a swim in the refreshingly cool water. It was also nice to sit on the raft and appreciate the beautiful nature around us. After the rafting, we made our way to Katzrin, where we had some yummy lunch and explored the town a bit. 

After that, we went to the meaningful sight of Tel Saki, where we learned about an impactful story from the Yom Kippur War that left us in awe. We saw old army tanks and trucks. From that spot, we could also see Syria. It was so special to be able to see the place where our ancestors once lived. Finally, we headed back to the hotel, where we had a very informative session from Mayan Leshem about geopolitics and Israel. We learned a lot about Israel’s current situation within the context of Middle Eastern politics. This day was both fun and meaningful, and we can’t wait for tomorrow!!

~ Joelle Dayan

 #SCAYoungAdults #StandWithIsrael #AmYisraelHai #mayanotisrael #birthrightisrael 🇮🇱

17887965996162833.caption:
Second day of the SCA Birthright trip was amazing! 

We started off with a yummy breakfast at the hotel, then headed on the bus to Safed! Ido, our amazing tour guide, began the drive with our Israeli slang of the day, שי המהרבו. This phrase is an abbreviation of the words מה רבו מעשיך ה׳, which directly translates to “How great are Your works, HaShem.” This shows our great appreciation for the amazing sights that HaShem opens our eyes to everyday! We related to this phrase as we traveled around Safed and took in the beautiful sights and its great views of surrounding cities. 

When we arrived at Safed, our tour guide explained the rich history, highlighting the great Rabbis who were buried in the area. We also visited an old cistern, where we sang some unifying songs. Next, we walked the streets of Safed to visit ancient shuls decorated with many beautiful chandeliers and bright colors. Then, we stopped for some lunch, including some Yemenite cuisine! 

After some free time to explore the art galleries in the area, we went to hear from Abraham Loewenthal, an Israeli Kabalah artist, who explained meaningful ideas of Kabalah, while speaking about his own art. After this enjoyable and education experience, we headed back on the bus to Savana Farm, where we picked some cherries and mulberries! Overall, we had an awesome day and can’t wait for tomorrow! 

~ Raquel Arakanchi

 #SCAYoungAdults #StandWithIsrael #AmYisraelHai #mayanotisrael #birthrightisrael 🇮🇱

18073015045746245.caption:
Our trip is off to a super strong start! We woke up on day one to a delicious Israeli-style breakfast, and had the chance to do some icebreakers with our fellow trip members to get to know each other a little better. Then we headed to זכרון יעקב to learn about Israel’s history and its early beginnings and advocators, including the history of the Aronson family and wealthy Rothschild family. We learned about the hardships they went through in order to provide the simplest resource to their community: accessible water. 

We then had the chance to shop around רחוב המיסדים with friends and have a free lunch together in the local authentic Israeli falafel shops. After that, we headed to a beautiful garden made by the Rothschild family, where we saw insane scenery including gardens, statues, and gravesites all emulating the idea that wealth is not determined by a tangible number, rather on what we give back to our community. 

As our day came to an end, we headed up north to Caesaria, where we saw an amphitheater you’d only see in a Roman movie, and visited the beach where we stood in the remains of amphitheaters and horse race tracks that Romans used to use for entertainment. We even had a race there of our own! We discussed the Roman exile story of the Jewish people, and even got a chance to see the apparent jail that Rabbi Akiva was put into for trying to heroically rebel against the Romans and stay true to his Judaism. Our day was packed with extremely impactful and eye opening experiences. Looking forward to day 2!
~ Linda Berkovitz

18066031132988814.caption: And that’s a wrap on the final day of #ChaiOnLife! The day kicked off with dancing in Gan Sacher alongside SY Olim @syisraelhome followed by a delicious brunch. From there, the group rolled up their sleeves for a @bohemianbalabusta cooking experience, preparing meals for soldiers’ families. In a full-circle moment, last year’s Chai On Life group met Sapir and had been praying for Sasha’s release ever since. #SCAIsrael #DoubleChai #StandWithIsrael

17856633276371023.caption:
Day 4 of #ChaiOnLife began with a refreshing morning at Sachne Springs, where the trip joined wives of miluim soldiers for games and swimming. In a powerful and unexpected moment, they crossed paths with @dintesler —a Nova Festival survivor. Din was on security duty during the attack and survived by hiding in a cactus for nine hours. His close friend, Bar Kupershtein, was kidnapped and remains in captivity.
That evening, they shared a fun dinner and cocktail workshop at Tipsey Cafe with more incredible miluim wives from Jerusalem.
#SCAIsrael #DoubleChai #StandWithIsrael

18306657097232959.caption: Day 3 of #DoubleChai started bright and early with a sunrise hike with the family of Yosef Guedalia - a solider who fell in Gaza. After lunch and a creative mosaic session with Michal Lubanov - the wife of Alex Lubonov @remember.alex.lobanov who was one of the six hostages killed at end of August 2024 - the group made their way to Tel Aviv for some relaxing time on the beach. They ended the day with a meaningful dinner at Regina Tel Aviv, joined by October 7th former hostage- Luis Har and his family #SCAIsrael #StandWithIsrael #ChaiOnLife

18031124495653404.caption: Only day one of the Double Chai Trip and these incredible women are already leaving a powerful mark. The morning began with breakfast and uplifting dancing alongside a group of widows, each of whom lost their husbands in the war. From there, they visited Kever Rachel with Elana Mizrachi, adding a meaningful spiritual moment to the day. The journey continued at the home of Joanna—a widow whose husband was killed in Lebanon—where they completely transformed her space. From new furniture to a deep clean, fully stocked kitchen, and thoughtful décor, they brought comfort, beauty, and hope back into her home. #SCAIsrael #ChaiOnLife #StandWithIsrael #DoubleChai

18068342536964117.caption: Chai on Life has landed in Israel! Just like last year, a group of incredible women, led by Shirley Catton, arrived in Israel with a shared mission: to make a meaningful difference. Upon landing, they visited the Kotel, followed by dinner at Brunch Cafe with Chef Zissie. There, they heard a powerful and heartbreaking story from Ella Mor. On October 7th, her three-year-old niece was taken hostage. Her nieces and nephews witnessed their parents’ murder and hid in a closet for 14 agonizing hours. Ella shared how, even in the face of unimaginable pain, she found strength by choosing action and moving forward. #DoubleChai #ChaiOnLife #StandWithIsrael #SCAIsrael

Last week we arranged for Professor Gil Troy, a member of SCA advisory board on campus antisemitism, to speak to students at four high schools.
. 
About Professor Gil Troy:
A distinguished scholar in North American History at McGill University currently living in Jerusalem, Gil Troy is an award-winning American presidential historian and a leading Zionist activist. He is the author of “To Resist the Academic Intifada: Letters to My Students on Defending the Zionist Dream.” Troy also published “The Essential Guide to October 7th and its Aftermath: Facts, Figures, History,” which has been translated in French and widely reprinted. Several years ago, he and Natan Sharansky co-authored Never Alone: Prison, Politics and My People. Recently designated an Algemeiner J-100, one of the top 100 people “positively influencing Jewish life, Troy has published essays in the American, Canadian, and Israeli media. Additionally, Gil is a member of SCA advisory board on campus antisemitism.

17849598636282802.caption:
As we approach Simhat Torah, Rabbi David Tawil of @larchwood_shul reflects on the mixed emotions we carry with us, one year after the barbaric attacks of October 7th. While we prepare to celebrate, we also remember the pain and loss endured by our people. Yet, through it all, our unity has only grown stronger. This Simhat Torah, we come together as one, embracing both the joy of the Hag and the strength we draw from standing together as a united community.

#SCAIsrael #SimhatTorah #UnityAndStrength #AmYisraelHai

17938188821919953.caption:
As we mark the Hebrew anniversary of October 7th this Simhat Torah, Rabbi Ikey Tawil of @kolisraelcongregation speaks about the emotional struggles we face one year later. He reminds us of the importance of our commitment to wear this pin as a silent remembrance of the fallen heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice on that tragic day. Through this simple act, we honor their memory and stand united in our resolve to never forget.

#SCAIsrael #SimhatTorah #SilentRemembrance #AmYisraelHai

18014199644342322.caption:
As we approach Simhat Torah, Rabbi Victor Mosseri of @shaareshalom reminds us why, even in the face of hardship, we still have reason to dance this year. While we hold on to the importance of remembering those we’ve lost and the challenges we face, we also embrace the joy that Simhat Torah brings. Our strength comes from this balance—celebrating while never forgetting the past. This year, we dance with both resilience and remembrance in our hearts.

#SCAIsrael #SimhatTorah #JoyAndRemembrance #AmYisraelHai

18084530185517338.caption:
As we approach Simhat Torah, Rabbi Joey Mizrahi of @bneiyitzhak reflects on the delicate balance between the extreme Simha (joy) required for the Hag and the solemn memory of last Simhat Torah, while our soldiers are still fighting and our hostages remain in Gaza. He reminds us that while we celebrate, we must also stand in unity with Am Yisrael, honoring both our joy and our ongoing struggle. This year, Congregation Bnei Yitzhak will be distributing over 500 pins as a symbol of that unity. Wear yours with pride, standing together with our brothers and sisters in Israel.

#SCAIsrael #SimhatTorah #UnityAndRemembrance #AmYisraelHai

18306465421165808.caption:

In this powerful video, he reminds us that through standing together, we find the resilience to face even the darkest times. Our unity is our strength, and this Simhat Torah, we honor those we’ve lost by continuing to stand as one people, with unwavering faith and hope.

#SCAIsrael #UnityAndStrength #SimhatTorah #AmYisraelHai

18087008386504223.caption:
As we approach Simhat Torah, the Hebrew anniversary of October 7th, Rabbi Joey Soffer of Congregation Beth Torah shares a meaningful reminder on how we can honor the memory of those we lost, while still embracing the joy of Yom Tob. #SCAIsrael #SimhatTorah #RemembranceAndResilience #AmYisraelHai

18048319732668145.caption:
Our final day of this incredible trip to Israel started off with a #ChaiOnLife class and delicious picnic brunch in Gan Sacher, Jerusalem specially organized for the women of our community who have made Aliyah. After a week of meeting and connecting with all different kinds of Israelis it was so special to share this morning with the women from our community who currently live in Israel by dancing and having fun! Next we met with Noah Lewis and heard about how she performs the ultimate hesed taking care of the bodies of female soldiers who fell in battle. 
We returned to the Inbal for a Hallah bake lead by Anat, @challah.mom where we danced with the Israeli flag and kneaded dough with  intention and love for soldiers. We had a quick dinner and headed to the airport with tears of joy, as our trip was so meaningful and memorable! @curlyshirleycatton #StandWithIsrael

18262419826241809.caption:
Day 3 of SCA #ChaiOnLife began with packaging food for our beloved IDF soldiers at Crave restaurant- which from the moment we entered turned into a full-on dance party with the staff and blasting Israeli music! After that we visited Hostage square and the wounded warriors at Tel Hashomer Hospital. The next stop was an epic Chai on Life experience where Shirley Catton led the group, joined by displaced women (and of course eager passerby’s as well) in her unique blend of dance, fitness and musical inspiration on the tayelet! We brought in the sunset and took a swim with the women in the ocean! The joy was truly contagious!
We met Eliya Attali a female combat paramedic that came back from Gaza to share her story and give us a peak into her life and how she defends her country. 
Tonight’s dinner was with an amazing group of IDF female soldiers. We were honored to also be joined by Sapir Cohen, a released hostage, (and her family)who’s tirelessly advocating for the release of her boyfriend Sasha Troufanov, who is still being held by Hamas. It was a very powerful and moving dinner. #StandWithIsrael

18037015375916491.caption: Today was a very special day that could only have been achieved by this unique group! It began super early with sunrise prayers and yoga in the desert. We heard from Idit Eliyahu about her son Ariel A”H and his bravery on October 7th. A few months ago our community (spearheaded by @barkaiyeshiva ) dedicated a grand piano in Ariel’s memory as he loved playing the piano. We played that piano and sang together- driving home the mission of our trip- bringing joy through music and movement. After a stop at the Dead Sea where we did a group float and some rest and relaxation exercises, we went for a delicious lunch at the Shuk. While there we went shopping for party supplies for the families who have been displaced since the beginning of the war. Our afternoon continued with pottery painting together with a group of displaced senior citizens from Kiryat Shmonah. Then we partied with women and children whose husbands and fathers are serving in the reserves- we played musical chairs and did arts and crafts, followed by pizza dinner and of course a #ChaiOnLife silent dance party. Can’t wait to continue the action tomorrow! @curlyshirleycatton #StandWithIsrael

Next- they visited Shokeda and heard from Chana about this community’s miraculous story of survival. Then they had the honor of meeting with the family of Yotam Haim A”H. In today’s world, showing our solidarity with Israel is more important than ever. The Sephardic Community Alliance invites you to visibly demonstrate your support by participating in our special campaign from Yom Hazikaron to Yom Yerushalayim. Join us in a united front by displaying a lawn sign that proudly proclaims your support for Israel.

How to Participate:
1. See link in bio to place your order: We are committed to making participation as easy as possible—sign up today, and we will deliver your sign to your doorstep at no cost.
2. Display Your Sign: Once you receive your sign, place it prominently in front of your home. By doing so, you are not only celebrating Israel’s past achievements and ongoing endeavors but also encouraging others in our community to stand in solidarity.
3. Share Your Support:
   - Capture the Moment: Once your sign is up, take a photo and share it on social media.
   - Tag Us: Post your picture on Instagram and tag the SCA. This helps spread the word and amplifies our collective voice.

Why It Matters:
Now, more than ever, it’s crucial to stand visibly and proudly with Israel. Through these signs, we send a powerful message of unity and resilience in the face of challenges. Your participation sends a clear signal of your commitment and encourages others to join in this important expression of support.
By sharing your installation on social media, you help foster a wider sense of community and activism. Let’s use our collective voice to celebrate the State of Israel and advocate for its future. Join us today — together, we make a difference

Disclaimer: This offer is limited to one lawn sign per household and is only available while supplies last. Currently, we are equipped to deliver only within the Brooklyn area. We appreciate your understanding and are excited to see your participation! #STANDWITHISRAEL 🇮🇱

18006659606237067.caption: This morning was undoubtedly the toughest part of the trip so far. We went to Kibutz Be’eri to bear witness to the inhumane atrocities that Hamas committed on October 7th. From there we went to Adi Negev, a school for disabled children, where we interacted with the kids. It was a really emotional first half of the day, but nonetheless we must be there for our brothers and sisters- in happy times and in sad times. Hineni. #StandWithIsrael #AmYisraelHai #SCAYoungAdults

17994444755240531.caption: We ended Day 3 of Hineni by throwing a barbecue for our soldiers. We were thrilled to be able to help prepare and serve the delicious food to our heroes. We danced and sang together and we got to know them and to hear about their experiences. Most importantly, we had the opportunity to tell them how much we support them and although we live on the other side of the world- express to them we are here together. Hineni. #AmYisraelHai #StandWithIsrael #SCAYoungAdults

18036084823634492.caption: This afternoon we returned to Lahav Farms where we resumed building the rehabilitation center for those traumatized by the events of October 7th. We then prayed Tehilim at a memorial by the farm for Adrienne Neta, a farm employee and nurse, who was brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists at her home in Kibbutz Be’eri. We hiked to the site of an ancient synagogue where we prayed Minha and when nightfall hit we bonded together over songs and bonfire lead by @rj2music (in a fire pit and on benches that we ourselves built!) Our work at Lahav Farm will be put to immediate use and have a lasting impact.  #AmYisraelHai #StandWithIsrael #SCAYoungAdults

17976034589499809.caption: This morning we visited a school in Yerucham that was set up for elementary aged kids from the Southern Kibbutzim who have been displaced since October 7th. Our young adults instantly connected to them- giving out toys and ice cream, playing sports and games and brought smiles to their faces. Special shoutout to Mia Horovitz for all the toys! We showed them that we’re in this together. Here we are. Hineni. #StandWithIsrael #amyisraelhai #SCAYoungAdults

18009769766283493.caption: Hineni Day 2- We spent most of today at Lahav Farm, where we began working on a new rehabilitation center, which will offer support to those traumatized by the October 7th massacres. We got to hear from the founder of the farm, Nir, who explained to us his personal motivations for wanting to help those affected by the trauma. These young adults were not afraid to get their handy dirty by building a deck and fireplace for outdoor therapy, burying utility cables, meticulously sanding surfaces, painting walls and so much more. After hours of rewarding work, we ended off the day sharing a delicious barbecue with IDF soldiers who just returned from Gaza at an army base. We ate with them and interacted with them, underscoring the sense of community and resilience that Israel is all about. Can’t wait to continue the action tomorrow! #StandWithIsrael #AmYisraelHai #SCAYoungAdults

18012492226900358.caption: Families from Kibutz Be’eri haven’t been home since October 7th. They’ve been displaced for 79 days and today we went to bring a smile to their faces. We threw them a carnival and  so that for a few hours, they can feel normal again, experience a glimpse of happiness and excitement. Popcorn, cotton candy, rides, singing, dancing, facepaint- then a special concert by E-Z. We showed them they are not alone. We are here. Hineni. #SCAYoungAdults

‎א  שִׁיר, לַמַּעֲלוֹת: אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי, אֶל-הֶהָרִים—    מֵאַיִן, יָבֹא עֶזְרִי. ב  עֶזְרִי, מֵעִם יְהוָה—    עֹשֵׂה, שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ. ג  אַל-יִתֵּן לַמּוֹט רַגְלֶךָ;    אַל-יָנוּם, שֹׁמְרֶךָ. ד  הִנֵּה לֹא-יָנוּם, וְלֹא יִישָׁן—    שׁוֹמֵר, יִשְׂרָאֵל. ה  יְהוָה שֹׁמְרֶךָ;    יְהוָה צִלְּךָ, עַל-יַד יְמִינֶךָ. ו  יוֹמָם, הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לֹא-יַכֶּכָּה;    וְיָרֵחַ בַּלָּיְלָה. ז  יְהוָה, יִשְׁמָרְךָ מִכָּל-רָע:    יִשְׁמֹר, אֶת-נַפְשֶׁךָ. ח  יְהוָה, יִשְׁמָר-צֵאתְךָ וּבוֹאֶךָ—    מֵעַתָּה, וְעַד-עוֹלָם.

‎ א  לַמְנַצֵּחַ, מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד. ב  יַעַנְךָ יְהוָה, בְּיוֹם צָרָה;    יְשַׂגֶּבְךָ, שֵׁם אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב. ג  יִשְׁלַח-עֶזְרְךָ מִקֹּדֶשׁ;    וּמִצִּיּוֹן, יִסְעָדֶךָּ. ד  יִזְכֹּר כָּל-מִנְחֹתֶךָ;    וְעוֹלָתְךָ יְדַשְּׁנֶה סֶלָה. ה  יִתֶּן-לְךָ כִלְבָבֶךָ;    וְכָל-עֲצָתְךָ יְמַלֵּא. ו  נְרַנְּנָה, בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ—    וּבְשֵׁם-אֱלֹהֵינוּ נִדְגֹּל; יְמַלֵּא יְהוָה,    כָּל-מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֶיךָ. ז  עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי—    כִּי הוֹשִׁיעַ יְהוָה, מְשִׁיחוֹ: יַעֲנֵהוּ, מִשְּׁמֵי קָדְשׁוֹ—    בִּגְבֻרוֹת, יֵשַׁע יְמִינוֹ. ח  אֵלֶּה בָרֶכֶב,    וְאֵלֶּה בַסּוּסִים; וַאֲנַחְנוּ,    בְּשֵׁם-יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ נַזְכִּיר. ט  הֵמָּה, כָּרְעוּ וְנָפָלוּ;    וַאֲנַחְנוּ קַּמְנוּ, וַנִּתְעוֹדָד. י  יְהוָה הוֹשִׁיעָה:    הַמֶּלֶךְ, יַעֲנֵנוּ בְיוֹם-קָרְאֵנוּ.

‎א  שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת:
‎מִמַּעֲמַקִּים קְרָאתִיךָ  יְהוָה.
‎ב  אֲדֹנָי,  שִׁמְעָה בְקוֹלִי:
‎תִּהְיֶינָה אָזְנֶיךָ, קַשֻּׁבוֹת—  לְקוֹל, תַּחֲנוּנָי.
‎ג  אִם-עֲוֺנוֹת תִּשְׁמָר-יָהּ— אֲדֹנָי, מִי יַעֲמֹד.
‎ד  כִּי-עִמְּךָ הַסְּלִיחָה—  לְמַעַן, תִּוָּרֵא.
‎ה  קִוִּיתִי יְהוָה, קִוְּתָה נַפְשִׁי;  וְלִדְבָרוֹ הוֹחָלְתִּי.
‎ו  נַפְשִׁי לַאדֹנָי—  מִשֹּׁמְרִים לַבֹּקֶר, שֹׁמְרִים לַבֹּקֶר.
‎ז  יַחֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶל-יְהוָה:  כִּי-עִם-יְהוָה הַחֶסֶד; וְהַרְבֵּה עִמּוֹ פְדוּת.
‎ח  וְהוּא, יִפְדֶּה אֶת-יִשְׂרָאֵל—  מִכֹּל, עֲוֺנֹתָיו.

‎א  לְדָוִד:    יְהוָה, אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי—מִמִּי אִירָא; יְהוָה מָעוֹז-חַיַּי,    מִמִּי אֶפְחָד. ב  בִּקְרֹב עָלַי, מְרֵעִים—    לֶאֱכֹל אֶת-בְּשָׂרִי: צָרַי וְאֹיְבַי לִי;    הֵמָּה כָשְׁלוּ וְנָפָלוּ. ג  אִם-תַּחֲנֶה עָלַי, מַחֲנֶה—    לֹא-יִירָא לִבִּי: אִם-תָּקוּם עָלַי, מִלְחָמָה—    בְּזֹאת, אֲנִי בוֹטֵחַ. ד  אַחַת, שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵאֵת-יְהוָה—    אוֹתָהּ אֲבַקֵּשׁ: שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית-יְהוָה,    כָּל-יְמֵי חַיַּי; לַחֲזוֹת בְּנֹעַם-יְהוָה,    וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ. ה  כִּי יִצְפְּנֵנִי, בְּסֻכֹּה—    בְּיוֹם רָעָה: יַסְתִּרֵנִי, בְּסֵתֶר אָהֳלוֹ;    בְּצוּר, יְרוֹמְמֵנִי. ו  וְעַתָּה יָרוּם רֹאשִׁי, עַל אֹיְבַי סְבִיבוֹתַי,    וְאֶזְבְּחָה בְאָהֳלוֹ, זִבְחֵי תְרוּעָה; אָשִׁירָה וַאֲזַמְּרָה,    לַיהוָה. ז  שְׁמַע-יְהוָה קוֹלִי אֶקְרָא;    וְחָנֵּנִי וַעֲנֵנִי. ח  לְךָ, אָמַר לִבִּי—בַּקְּשׁוּ פָנָי;    אֶת-פָּנֶיךָ יְהוָה אֲבַקֵּשׁ. ט  אַל-תַּסְתֵּר פָּנֶיךָ, מִמֶּנִּי—    אַל תַּט-בְּאַף, עַבְדֶּךָ: עֶזְרָתִי הָיִיתָ;    אַל-תִּטְּשֵׁנִי וְאַל-תַּעַזְבֵנִי, אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׁעִי. י  כִּי-אָבִי וְאִמִּי עֲזָבוּנִי;    וַיהוָה יַאַסְפֵנִי. יא  הוֹרֵנִי יְהוָה, דַּרְכֶּךָ:    וּנְחֵנִי, בְּאֹרַח מִישׁוֹר—לְמַעַן, שׁוֹרְרָי. יב  אַל-תִּתְּנֵנִי, בְּנֶפֶשׁ צָרָי:    כִּי קָמוּ-בִי עֵדֵי-שֶׁקֶר, וִיפֵחַ חָמָס. יג  לוּלֵא—הֶאֱמַנְתִּי, לִרְאוֹת בְּטוּב-יְהוָה:    בְּאֶרֶץ חַיִּים. יד  קַוֵּה, אֶל-יְהוָה:    חֲזַק, וְיַאֲמֵץ לִבֶּךָ; וְקַוֵּה, אֶל-יְהוָה.

א  לַמְנַצֵּחַ, מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד.
ב  הַשָּׁמַיִם, מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד-אֵל;  וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו, מַגִּיד הָרָקִיעַ.
ג  יוֹם לְיוֹם, יַבִּיעַ אֹמֶר;  וְלַיְלָה לְּלַיְלָה, יְחַוֶּה-דָּעַת.
ד  אֵין-אֹמֶר, וְאֵין דְּבָרִים:  בְּלִי, נִשְׁמָע קוֹלָם.
ה  בְּכָל-הָאָרֶץ, יָצָא קַוָּם,  וּבִקְצֵה תֵבֵל, מִלֵּיהֶם;
לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, שָׂם-אֹהֶל בָּהֶם.
ו  וְהוּא—כְּחָתָן, יֹצֵא מֵחֻפָּתוֹ; יָשִׂישׂ כְּגִבּוֹר, לָרוּץ אֹרַח.
ז  מִקְצֵה הַשָּׁמַיִם, מוֹצָאוֹ—וּתְקוּפָתוֹ עַל-קְצוֹתָם;  וְאֵין נִסְתָּר, מֵחַמָּתוֹ.
ח  תּוֹרַת יְהוָה תְּמִימָה, מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ; עֵדוּת יְהוָה נֶאֱמָנָה, מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי.
ט  פִּקּוּדֵי יְהוָה יְשָׁרִים, מְשַׂמְּחֵי-לֵב;  מִצְוַת יְהוָה בָּרָה, מְאִירַת עֵינָיִם.
י  יִרְאַת יְהוָה, טְהוֹרָה—עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד:  מִשְׁפְּטֵי-יְהוָה אֱמֶת; צָדְקוּ יַחְדָּו.
יא  הַנֶּחֱמָדִים—מִזָּהָב, וּמִפַּז רָב;  וּמְתוּקִים מִדְּבַשׁ, וְנֹפֶת צוּפִים.
יב  גַּם-עַבְדְּךָ, נִזְהָר בָּהֶם;  בְּשָׁמְרָם, עֵקֶב רָב.
יג  שְׁגִיאוֹת מִי-יָבִין;  מִנִּסְתָּרוֹת נַקֵּנִי.
יד  גַּם מִזֵּדִים, חֲשֹׂךְ עַבְדֶּךָ— אַל-יִמְשְׁלוּ-בִי אָז אֵיתָם;
וְנִקֵּיתִי,  מִפֶּשַׁע רָב.
טו  יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי-פִי, וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי  לְפָנֶיךָ:
יְהוָה,  צוּרִי וְגֹאֲלִי.

17874849923818806.caption:
“Sacred Time” as told by Rabbi Joseph Beyda

When I consider the idea of ‘Renewable Energy’, I am immediately drawn to a story Rabbi Sacks used to share.
Rabbi Sacks once took a childcare expert, Dr Penelope Leach, to a Jewish primary school, and showed her the five-year-old children rehearsing for the Shabbat dinner table. She asked one of the children what he most liked about Shabbat. He replied, “It’s the only time of the week when daddy doesn’t have to rush off.”
As they left the school, she turned to Rabbi Sacks and said, “That Sabbath of yours (Penelope isn’t Jewish) is saving their parents’ marriages.” He agreed with her. As he mentions in one of his books, “Families need time, and Shabbat is sacred, dedicated time.” (The Home We Build Together, pp. 213-214)

As someone who worked in both a Jewish Day School and in a pulpit position at the same time, the idea of the stress of work taking away from family time really resonated with me. Both of my jobs could seem all-consuming at times. There’s no doubt that some of the time I could and should have spent with my family was compromised. I am thankful to Shabbat for making sacred time for my family.
I am likewise grateful to Rabbi Sacks for emphasising to me the importance of family, and the need to carve out time for them no matter how busy my schedule might get.
______
This new series of Covenant & Conversation: Family Editions features one new voice each week. We hope that this will further illuminate the ideas of Rabbi Sacks and encourage others to continue these conversations with the next generation, as we share the stories and ideas of Rabbi Sacks scholars.
Rabbi Joseph Beyda is the Head of School of the Yeshivah of Flatbush Joel Braverman High School in Brooklyn, where he lives with his wife and six children.

17981061850577858.caption:
This past Thursday night we had the honor in partnering with The Tikvah Fund in hosting world acclaimed author Dara Horn, whose most recent book is titled “People Love Dead Jews”. 

Prior to the event, select young adults (many of whom are #SCABootCampUs graduates!) had the opportunity to meet with Dara and discuss the importance of maintaining a strong sense of Jewish identity on their college campuses. 

Following that discussion, SCA Trustee Mr. Ronny Hersh introduced the night. He highlighted the importance of the SCA to act as resource for the community to engage with different organizations which create opportunities for important discussions and causes that impact the larger Jewish community. We were privileged to have Rabbi Dr. Ricky Hidary lead a thought provoking discussion with Dara, part of which included the challenges of preserving Jewish History and Jewish identity throughout time. After the conversation, we opened the floor to a riveting Q & A session from the crowd and a book signing. 

Thank you to Regine and Jack Ashkenazie for opening up their home and for their continued partnership with the SCA! We also thank everyone who helped make this event possible!

17915206778455875.caption:
No better way to end off BootCampUs than a custom made activity like The Amazing Race! The students were split into four teams- shawarma, shakshuka, shish kabob and schnitzel- and competed against each other, combining teamwork and stamina to overcome obstacles along with solving puzzles and trivia based on the material they learned for their team to advance. Highlights included human bowling, rock climbing, deconstructing an Israeli salad and so much more! Everyone had a blast at this race. Special thank you to @curlyshirleycatton for spearheading this and to @richiedweck for ensuring this crazy race went off without a hitch!
.
@welovemdyhs @hillelyeshiva @yofhs @ramazschool @frischschool @yeshivahprep

17873330159673125.caption:
We must give a HUGE thank you to @standwithus for supporting us on our first annual Boot CampUs! The intimate discussion sessions lead by multiple representatives were one of our favorites. They were a great way for BootCampers to connect with current activists who are facing many of the challenges that our students may face in the future! Thank you for all your support and leading the way in education on Israel.
.
@welovemdyhs @hillelyeshiva @yofhs @ramazschool @frischschool @yeshivahprep

SCA BootCampUs 2022 is sponsored by Sharyn & Ezra S. Ashkenazi in honor of Nava and Jeffrey Beyda

17936899319046826.caption:
The third and final day of SCA BootCampUs began by hearing from Sefi Kraut, Director of Education for the Pardes Mahloket Matters Schools project. She facilitated an interactive session highlighting the importance of different viewpoints on all subject matter. “Makhloket” is rooted in our Jewish tradition, teaching us that all opinions matter and should be respected. Learning the value of a constructive disagreement mindset will hopefully enhance our bootcampers experience on the college campus and beyond!  Next was a talk titled “Why am I a Zionist” by @Jewishunpacked . They showed us the many resources OpenDor Media has available for students to continue to further their education on Israel. Avi Posen showed us the new short film Open Spaces we were the first group to ever see it! 
.
@welovemdyhs @hillelyeshiva @yofhs @ramazschool @frischschool @yeshivahprep
.
SCA BootCampUs 2022 is sponsored by Sharyn & Ezra S. Ashkenazi in honor of Nava and Jeffrey Beyda

Earlier today, @yairlapid named her the FIRST-EVER Special Envoy for Combating Antisemitism and Delegitimization. 17901605708409857.caption:
Last night @sephardicrabbinicalcollege celebrated their siyum on “Amira LeGoy on Shabbat”!

Under the leadership of Rabbi Harold Sutton and spearheaded by Mr. Ovadia Sutton, this group started a little over a year ago when these young men decided to take it upon themselves to truly understand topics in Halakha. When learning a topic, they learn the Sugyot in the Gemara, the Rishonim, Tur, Bet Yosef, Shulhan Arukh and Aharonim. They don’t just learn the material- they own it. They meet in Habrutot multiple times a week in preparation for their in person Shiurim, which take place Wednesday nights, Sunday mornings and Friday mornings. In Shiur is where they review all of the materials together with R Joey Soffer- the head of this program.

Last night’s Siyum (hosted by Eileen & Isaac Dweck) was their third Siyum together- the first was on Hilkhot Bishool and the second was on Hilkhot Mukse (swipe for pictures of previous Siyumim). For more information about this program contact R Soffer at (917) 365-6900

[Pictured at last night’s Siyum L-R: Joe Braha, Raymond Braha, Ralph Chattah, Albert Terzi, Rabbi Joey Soffer, Isaac Dweck, Eddie Farhi, Teddy Beyda & Jacob Franco]

17927471962921622.caption:
Earlier today SCA partnered with OpenDor Media to bring yet another amazing program to our community. Avi Posen, Assistant Director of Education at OpenDor Media, taught a one hour in depth session about antisemitism to our young men studying in Israel for the year at @moreshet_yerushalayim 
.
Because antisemitism isn’t always blatant and clear, young adults don’t always realize how deep it runs. They often need help acknowledging, recognizing and understanding antisemitism. Therefore, this interactive presentation was dedicated to unpacking the deep question of “Is Criticizing Israel Antisemitic?" The students learnt how to recognize antisemitism and now understand how it affects Jewish identity and community.
.
This program was generously sponsored by Ezra S. & Sharyn Ashkenazi

@rj2music newest single! 

The Ramban teaches that through studying and appreciating the grand miracles we can come to notice and appreciate the “smaller” ones. 

The time of Hanukkah is one of those amazing miracles that we will be celebrating, commemorating, and appreciating this week. But when we say Al Hanisim in our tefilot we not only mention the miracle of the Hanukkah, we praise Hashem for ALL of the miracles He did and continues to do for us Bayamim Hahem Bazman Hazeh, in those days and in our time. 
The song Al Hanisim takes us through the history of our amazing nation, from our patriarch Avraham Avinu until today. The idea is to help us visualize the awesome love that Hashem has for us throughout all of the generations, and open our eyes to the “smaller miracles" he does for each of us.... every single day.

Guide to at home Sukkot Prayers By: Rabbi David M. Tawil
￼￼The holiday of Sukkot is known as "זמן שמחתנו"- the time of our joy, and the prayers reflect this theme throughout. We recite the full Hallel with blessings each day. The Hoshanot are a unique ceremony to Sukkot, where we circle the Torah as a show of love for Hashem and His Torah. Except for Shabbat, we pray with our Lulav & Etrog. There are many special Misvot and prayers from which one can grow and inspire meaning in his/her life. Take advantage of this special time, whether in Synagogue or at home. The guide below is a support to help those praying from home get the most out of their prayers. The pages follow the HEBREW SHELOM YERUSHALAYIM MAHZOR. See link in bio to print

Guide for at home Yom Kippur Prayers By: Rabbi David M. Tawil
￼￼￼While praying with a Minyan is certainly an important and praiseworthy deed it does not supecede the requirement to stay safe and help keep others safe. As a result of the uptick in Covid-19 cases throughout the country and community, many are taking the proper steps to limit the spread by quarantining during this time. As a result, many will be alone at home on the day of Yom Kippur. One can fulfill majority of the prayer requirements on the day of Yom Kippur from their home. This guide will help those praying from home either along or with their families to navigate the prayers and fulfill their responsibilities. May Hashem keep us all safe and in the merit of our prayers, both public and private, heal those who are sick and stop this terrible virus from plaguing the world once and for all.

[SWIPE 👉🏻👉🏻] The following was written this weekend by SCA board member Ricky Novick: 

“Grateful to the IDF”
.
Rachel and I are really grateful to the IDF on so many levels. With the corona pandemic, Israel isn’t allowing non Israeli citizens into the country, except for families of a bride or groom, families of lone soldiers and others with extenuating circumstances. We feel blessed that we received permission to enter the country and are able to spend 10 weeks in Israel (through the holidays) for this once in a lifetime opportunity. The army gave our son Binyamin 10 days off and I just dropped him at the bus stop to go back to base after spending 10 days with him.

Before these past 10 days, the last time we hugged him was a year ago when when we dropped him at JFK airport to join the IDF. Maya Shaposhnik Cadena, AIPAC’s Sephardic division leader, told me say goodbye to my son forever, because the next time I’ll see him again, he will be a man. 

He surprised us last Wednesday night when the army let him off a day early. He came in full army uniform with his gun. Our family was shocked and just so happy to see him! After having a hot meal for the first time in a long time, he went to take a shower. He is taught to keep his gun on him at all times. When he goes to the bathroom and when he sleeps, the gun is by his side.

Spending the past 10 days with my son, I gained a new perspective and appreciation of the IDF. (Continued in comments)

FROM THE DOCTORS OF
OUR COMMUNITY
​ ​ 
UPDATE ON RESURGENCE OF COVID-19
IN OUR COMMUNITY
Although the low number of new cases over the last few months created the possibility for summer events and larger gatherings, it’s become clear over the last few days that the virus remains extremely contagious and active within our community. Over the past five days, there has been an alarming uptick of confirmed Covid-19 infections in our community, primarily in the Deal, NJ area, but also some in Brooklyn, NY. We must remain vigilant.
At the same time that we see an increase in cases within our community, we also see a rapid and dramatic increase of new infections in many states around the country, a somber reminder of how quickly and silently this virus can spread. Therefore we urge all community members to remain vigilant and double their efforts in fighting the spread of Covid-19 by taking the following unified actions: 
• Maintain social distancing
• Adhere to mask-wearing when social distancing is not possible (now required both indoors and outdoors by NJ state law)
• Wash hands frequently
• Avoid large gatherings where social distancing is not possible
• Indoor gatherings of any size pose a far greater risk than outdoor gatherings, and should be avoided as much as possible
• Continue to exercise extreme caution if you are over the age of 65, are immunocompromised, have pre-existing medical conditions, live with or find yourself in proximity to any individuals that are at higher risk of becoming gravely ill should they become infected 
[continued in comments]

RePosted • @ujafedny What you're about to read is difficult, but even amid these unimaginable circumstances, we must continue to provide dignity and respect to those around us — including those we have lost.⠀
-⠀
We've suffered tremendous loss due to this crisis and many have passed away alone, without family or friends to kiss them goodbye and whisper words of love. So when we can no longer sustain life, how do we help those who are desperately seeking to honor the dead?⠀
-⠀
Faced with this deepest heartbreak, we must do all we can to ease the suffering of those grieving. A dignified burial is one of the greatest services we can offer during this time. That's why we're helping the Hebrew Free Burial Association accommodate every single request it has received, to ensure that every Jew regardless of financial means or religious affiliation, can receive a dignified, traditional funeral and burial — the ultimate final kindness.⠀
-⠀
Pictured: Rabbi Levi Gurkov of Chabad of Oceanside, NY, wearing a hazmat suit to perform a burial; 70 beautiful tallitot generously donated by @sca_updates.

18104205100107008.caption:
🇮🇱 The polls are open! 🇮🇱 .
.
With dozens of organizations trying to capture YOUR vote for this year’s Word Zionist Congress (WZC), we pulled together a list of the slates that our affiliate organizations have been endorsing and promoting for election. It is imperative that we hit the polls to ensure that we have strong representation in the next WZC. Please carefully review the slides above and find your preference before the deadline closes on March 11, 2020. .
.
🇮🇱 About WZC 🇮🇱 .
.
The 38th World Zionist Congress (WZC) will be held in Jerusalem from October 20 – 22, 2020. It is the only democratically elected global Jewish forum and is the direct continuation of The First Zionist Congress, convened by Theodor Herzl in 1897. That gathering was the genesis of the modern Zionist movement and the original meeting of great minds that collectively put to paper the idea that the Jewish people should have a state of their own. Today, the WZC, which now meets about every five years, is the overall supreme ideological and policy-making body of the Zionist movement. The delegates and the bodies they form at the WZC determine the leadership and influence the policies of Israel’s National Institutions: the World Zionist Organization (WZO), the Jewish Agency for Israel (JAFI), Jewish National Fund-Keren Kayemet LeIsrael (JNF) and Keren Hayesod – which together allocate nearly $1 billion annually in funding in support of Israel and Jewish communities around the world.
.
.

For more information on the WZC , please visit www.zionistelection.org
.
.
@wzo.official
#WorldZionistCongress
#ZionistElection
#DreamWZO

18063649792170825.caption:
A bit of history behind the name of member affiliate organization “Allegra Franco School of Educational Leadership” that has trained so many community teachers over the years! Follow @sephardicheritagemuseum to learn about more amazing people and the history of our community 
Posted @withrepost • @sephardicheritagemuseum “I am artistically inclined. I love to sew and make beautiful hats of different shapes from different materials to fit each individual’s face and colors to blend.” - Allegra (Ashear) Franco a’h born 1900. Passed away 2000. 
Allegra Franco was ahead of her time in many ways. As a young woman, she was involved in real estate and sales. In the years before the Depression, she owned her own business, a Millinery store named the Allegra Shoppe. (Note the store name on the window!) At the time that she was running the Allegra Shoppe, the law was that stores must close on Sunday. Being that Allegra observed Shabbat she was unable to work on Saturday and would therefore lose money being closed for two consecutive days. 
She defied the law and opened her shop on Sundays. When law officers came to check in on her she boldly defended herself. “I will not open my doors on my Sabbath, therefore I have no option other than to remain open on Sunday!” The officers were no match for this determined, devout woman so they turned around and left. They never bothered her again. Slide ➡️ for more beautiful pics. #syrianjews #sephardicjews #jewishmuseum #jewishhistory #francofamily #ashearfamily #rabbimosesashear

Never Forget!

@safra_synagogue_nyc will be hosting a special screening of the remarkable film "Hidden" released by Project Witness.
Join @rabbishlomofarhi afterwards for a Q & A with the film's director Gi Orman.

Not to be missed!

This film takes the audience on a fascinating, harrowing, and emotional journey through the fateful years of the war when tens of thousands of children took on new, unfamiliar identities in hope of surviving the German onslaught. It brings survivors back to their childhood homes in Poland for first-hand interviews and dramatic reunions with their “adopted” families. This a must-see for anyone who cares about our rich heritage.

Tomorrow night, Thursday May 2nd 7:30PM.

[SWIPE 👉🏻👉🏻] We regret to announce the passing of David "DJ" Cohen. DJ was diagnosed 4 years ago today with stage 4 cancer. Despite it all, DJ’s trademark smile and upbeat attitude were never dimmed. He became determined to inspire and uplift all those he would come in contact with. He would show up to treatment sessions dressed up in funny costumes, turning the tables and cheering up his doctors, nurses and multitudes of visitors. He frequently spent time visiting other sick patients, lending an open ear. He wrote beautiful poetry and music, and sang from the heart to share with us his inner strength.

At the annual SCA Tisha’a B’Ab program, DJ (pictured above), would inspire and entertain, all while passing on invaluable life lessons to his beloved community. (The link to this specific class is on YouTube and in our bio.)
His contributions to our community and the entire world will never be forgotten. 
#TeamDeej

Funeral will take place Bloomfield Cooper, Thursday at 10:00 am 
Wife: Alexis Cohen Children: Linda, Lori, Caroline 
Parents: Linda and Judah Cohen 
Siblings: Robyn Adjmi, Sarah Gammal, and Ike Cohen

[SWIPE 👉🏻👉🏻] Today, November 30th, is annual “Jewish Refugee Day”. .
.
On November 29, 1947 the UN resolution on the partition of Palestine was announced. The following day, anti Zionistic riots spread throughout Arab lands, burning homes, businesses, synagogues and Jewish artifacts. Many Jews were murdered, forced to hide, or escaped permanently. These families had been in these lands for hundreds and even thousands have years prior. Life in the Middle East was never the same for Jews since then with humiliation, killings and persecutions to follow.  Today, November 30, is the day set aside by the State of Israel to commemorate the expulsion of 850,000 Jews of Arab lands since 1947.
.
.
We encourage all to take a moment either with their family at the Shabbat table or with a colleague in Synagogue to discuss the importance of remembering this day in history
.
.

17909240329153279.caption: Ordered in April 1945 by the Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force, German Concentration Camps Factual Survey is an official documentary about the atrocities committed at concentration camps under Nazi leadership. Producer Sidney Bernstein assembled a team at the Ministry of Information that included editors Stewart McAllister and Peter Tanner, writers Colin Wills and Richard Crossman; and Alfred Hitchcock who gave directorial advice. A compilation of footage shot by combat and newsreel cameramen accompanying troops as they liberated occupied Europe, the film was to be screened in Germany after the fall of the Third Reich – shown to German prisoners of war wherever they were held but was ultimately shelved before completion due to a shift in the priorities of the British government. German Concentration Camps Factual Survey is distributed in the United States by 3 Generations.

Tomorrow night @americansephardifederation is showing the most recent episode of @sephardicheritagemuseum! To purchase tickets, visit ASFSyrian.bpt.me
.

TUESDAY, MARCH 6TH AT 7 PM: THE SYRIAN SEPHARDIC COMMUNITY
.
.
The Syrian Jewish Community: Our Journey Through History THE JEWS OF SYRIA, 1930-1967
.
.
Directed by Lisa Ades
Executive Produced by Joseph J. Sitt
Documentary Feature, 90 min, USA, 2014, English
.
.
From Executive Producer, Joseph J. Sitt, the sixth installment of his multi-part series on the Syrian Sephardi community, is the fascinating story of life in Syria for the Jews who remained there after the massive exodus to the US and other countries in the early 1900s. Weaving together stories of pogroms and fires in Aleppo and Damascus in 1947 and 1948, of repression and heroic escapes as Jews in Syria, Lebanon, and Egypt fled persecution, the mysterious Aleppo Codex (part of which was smuggled to safety in Israel), the courageous Rabbi Abraham Kalmanowitz who helped Syrian boys escape to New York, and the Jewish spy, Elie Cohen, who helped his brothers in Israel win the Six Day War before his capture and execution, this is an incredible film about one of the Jewish People’s oldest and most illustrious communities.
.
.
